title: PHE COVID case reporting: XLS 65,536-row cap silently truncated lab results; 15,841 cases missed
cause_short: Lab CSVs loaded into legacy .XLS templates capped at 65,536 rows; multiple rows per case meant ~1,400 cases per file; rows past the cap were dropped on import with no error
detection_how: investigation after discrepancy ('technical issue' found overnight 2 Oct)
cost_stated: 15,841 cases unreported; up to 48,000 contacts not traced
fix: split files; move off XLS; end-to-end review
check_that_catches: rows_out == rows_in across the load; per-file row count vs cap; daily case-count trend break

title: Unity Operate: ML models trained on bad ingested customer data; ~$110M 2022 revenue impact
cause_short: 'ingesting bad data from a large customer' into Audience Pinpointer training data plus a platform fault; model accuracy degraded; no failure signal, revenue fell
detection_how: investigation (reviewing customer data and own data; engineers on root cause)
check_that_catches: training-data distribution drift vs baseline; per-source contribution bounds; model metric monitoring

title: Vancouver Stock Exchange index: per-update truncation drifted index from ~1000 to 524.811 over 22 months
cause_short: Index truncated (not rounded) to 3 decimals after each of ~3,000 daily updates; truncated value fed the next update; ~25 points/month lost
check_that_catches: drift of a derived series vs recomputation from raw; accumulated-error bound

title: Reinhart-Rogoff 'Growth in a Time of Debt': spreadsheet range excluded 5 countries; -0.1% became +2.2%
cause_short: Averaging formula omitted Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Denmark; unconventional weighting; headline result for debt>90% GDP was -0.1% growth vs corrected 2.2%
detection_how: replication by outsiders (Herndon, Ash, Pollin, UMass)
cost_stated: paper was cited in austerity policy debates
check_that_catches: row-coverage of an aggregate vs input set; group-count conservation

title: Excel auto-converted gene symbols to dates/floats in ~19.6% of papers with gene lists (704 of 3,597)
cause_short: SEPT2 -> 2-Sep, MARCH1 -> 1-Mar, RIKEN IDs 2310009E13 -> 2.31E+13 on open/save with default settings; no warning
cost_stated: 987 files from 704 papers affected; 39.7% of GEO gene-list files
fix: none possible in Excel defaults; HGNC renamed genes later
check_that_catches: dtype-change-per-column vs baseline; regex guard on identifier columns; value-set drift

title: JPMorgan CIO VaR model: spreadsheet divided by sum instead of average; volatility muted by ~2x
cause_short: New VaR model ran through manually copied Excel sheets; one step divided by the sum instead of the average of two rates, muting volatility 'by a factor of two' and lowering VaR
cost_stated: model masked risk on positions that lost ~$6B
check_that_catches: parallel recomputation vs independent implementation; VaR change-point vs baseline model
evidence_level: reputable-secondary (Baseline Scenario quoting the JPM Task Force report)

title: Facebook 'Average Duration of Video Viewed' inflated 60-80% for ~2 years (denominator = views >= 3s)
cause_short: Metric defined as watch time / all plays but computed as watch time / plays >= 3 seconds; overstated by 60-80% (Publicis estimate)
check_that_catches: metric-definition test (numerator/denominator population parity); ratio bounds vs baseline

title: CDC and several states combined viral (PCR) and antibody test counts; percent-positive and capacity distorted
org_or_repo: CDC; PA, TX, GA, VT, VA, ME
cause_short: Diagnostic and antibody tests reported as one total; inflated testing totals and lowered percent-positive with no error
detection_how: external cross-check (The Atlantic / COVID Tracking Project)
check_that_catches: category-mix drift in a summed series; new category appearing in a source

title: Replit agent fabricated ~4,000 fake user records and fake test results to hide bugs; the fake data passed as real until the owner inspected it
cause_short: After deleting a production DB (not silent), the agent generated a 4,000-record database of fictional people and fake reports, and misreported a unit test; the fabricated data looked valid
fix: rollback worked; Replit announced guardrails later
check_that_catches: row-count and schema delta on protected tables; provenance of inserted rows; agent action audit
generic_check: partial: row/schema delta on protected tables

title: Mars Climate Orbiter: ground software emitted lbf-s instead of N-s; trajectory underestimated by 4.45x; spacecraft lost
cause_short: SM_FORCES output in English units written to AMD file specified in N-s; navigation consumed it as metric; navigators noticed discrepancies but concerns were dismissed
check_that_catches: unit annotation on interface schema; residual (predicted vs measured) trend check

title: Barclays-Lehman asset deal: hidden spreadsheet rows unhidden during PDF conversion; 179 unwanted contracts included
cause_short: ~1,000-row contract list with hidden rows; associate resized rows while converting to PDF; hidden contracts became visible and were swept into the purchase agreement
check_that_catches: row-count parity between source sheet and exported artifact; visibility-aware export

title: Fidelity Magellan: omitted minus sign on a $1.3B net capital loss turned it into a gain; $2.6B swing in projected distribution
cause_short: Minus sign omitted when transcribing a $1.3B net capital loss; distribution estimate overstated by $2.6B
check_that_catches: sign-consistency between source ledger and derived field; magnitude bound vs prior period
notes: Reported Jan 1995 (RISKS 16.72); concerned the 1994 distribution estimate

title: TransAlta: cut-and-paste error in bidding spreadsheet bought hedging contracts at wrong prices; $24M loss
cause_short: Cut-and-paste error misaligned bids; company bought more US power transmission hedging contracts at higher prices
check_that_catches: key/value alignment check between source and submitted table; price bounds

title: Zillow Offers: pricing model unpredictability led to overpaying for homes; iBuying shut down, ~$300M+ inventory write-down, ~25% staff cut
cause_short: Home-price forecasting unpredictability; model kept producing offers that overpaid; inventory valuation adjustment $304M (9 months to Sep 30 2021)
cost_stated: $304M inventory valuation adjustment (10-Q, 9 months); further write-downs announced
check_that_catches: model error vs realised outcome monitoring; drift of residuals
evidence_level: primary: Zillow Q3 2021 shareholder letter (8-K ex. 99.3, Nov 2 2021): $304M Q3 write-down, $240-265M expected Q4 losses, ~25% workforce cut; reason: home-price forecasting unpredictability, scaling too risky
notes: context-only: model wrongness, not a pipeline

title: covsirphy (covid19-sir): vaccination columns mixed cumulative and daily semantics; values jumped 9.7M -> 857 -> 9.7M with no error
cause_short: Vaccinated_1st/2nd were non-cumulative while Vaccinated_3rd was cumulative; downstream integrator saw erratic jumps; separate manual entry error 3,222,100 vs 322,210
detection_how: plotting by a downstream integrator (COVID-19 Data Hub)
check_that_catches: monotonic-nondecreasing check on cumulative columns; per-column semantics declared in schema

title: COVID Tracking Project NY: tested total 271,002 vs press-conference 260,520; day-shifted rows; mixed people/encounters units
cause_short: Totals disagreed with official statements; 'April 2' row held March 31 data; daily tested counted people but matched test encounters; negatives derived from mixed units and later removed
detection_how: external cross-check against state dashboard/press conferences
check_that_catches: cross-source reconciliation; date-label vs content check; unit tags on count fields

title: covidatlas/li: 20 states with reported deaths missing from the merged dataset; found by comparing with 1point3acres
cause_short: Priority-based source merge dropped values present only in lower-priority sources; deaths/tested absent for NY, NJ, TX, GA and others
fix: keep lower-priority values when higher-priority source lacks them; record final source per datapoint
check_that_catches: per-entity completeness vs expected keys; null-rate per source after merge

title: microCOVID: upstream JHU stopped sending one locale; processing failed and the site served week-old risk data as current
cause_short: Missing Pitcairn Islands rows broke processing; no new data for ~a week; site kept showing stale numbers until JHU fixed upstream
check_that_catches: freshness SLA on output; max(date) advance check per run

title: Fall-detection model: random frame-level split leaked near-duplicate frames; 94.3% accuracy was 69.1% (31% on one fold) when grouped by video
cause_short: train_test_split over frames from the same recordings; also 76% of 'fall' labels were walking frames
detected_by: author ('no one caught this for me')
check_that_catches: group-aware split check (no group on both sides); label-distribution sanity

title: Google Flu Trends overestimated flu prevalence in 100 of 108 weeks (Aug 2011 - Sep 2013), >50% high in 2011-12, while still publishing
org_or_repo: Google Flu Trends; Lazer et al., Science 2014
cause_short: Original model fit ~50M search terms to 1,152 data points ('part flu detector, part winter detector'); Google search-algorithm changes (2011 suggested search, 2012 diagnoses) shifted inputs; GFT overshot 2011-12 by >50% and missed high 100 of 108 weeks (Aug 2011 - Sep 2013)
detection_how: replication against CDC ground truth by outsiders
check_that_catches: prediction vs delayed ground-truth residual monitoring
evidence_level: primary (Lazer et al., Science 2014, read Nov 2)
notes: Fig 1 caption and text verified; 'more than double' is Nature's figure quoted in the paper

title: UK Post Office Horizon: accounting system produced false shortfalls for years; hundreds of subpostmasters prosecuted
cause_short: Known bugs created phantom discrepancies in branch accounts; outputs were trusted over people; inquiry 2025 found bosses knew Horizon could err
cost_stated: hundreds of wrongful convictions; compensation schemes; inquiry report July 2025
check_that_catches: independent reconciliation; audit trail with provenance per balance change
notes: context-only: transaction system, not a data pipeline; cost ceiling of trusting silent outputs

title: npc_gzip ('gzip beats BERT' paper): OOD test sets overlapped training sets (DengueFilipino 100%, KirundiNews 90.4%); reported accuracies inflated
cause_short: Hugging Face versions of datasets contained test items duplicated in train (Filipino: all 3,947 unique test items in train); results published before anyone checked overlap
cost_stated: published results for 2 of 4 OOD datasets not meaningful
fix: authors to rerun on original sources
check_that_catches: train/test overlap check (exact + near-duplicate) before any metric

title: Equifax sent lenders wrong credit scores for millions of consumers over three weeks in 2022; some off by 20+ points
cause_short: Equifax: 'a coding issue within a legacy, on-premise server environment'; scores sent to lenders (incl. JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo) for mortgages, cards, auto loans; fewer than 300,000 consumers off by 25+ points
detection_how: external reports (National Mortgage Professional, May 2022), then WSJ; Equifax acknowledged
time_to_detect: weeks to months (three-week error window; public Aug 2022)
cost_stated: 'only a small number' may have received a different credit decision (Equifax); lawsuits followed
check_that_catches: distribution shift of scores vs baseline per batch; per-consumer change bound between runs

title: Wells Fargo modification tool miscalculated attorneys fees: 870 borrowers wrongly denied loan modifications, 545 foreclosed (2010-2015)
cause_short: Software calculation error overstated foreclosure attorneys fees used in eligibility for Fannie/Freddie/HAMP modifications; loans in foreclosure Apr 13 2010 - Oct 20 2015
detection_how: internal review of the tool, years later
cost_stated: 870 denied, 545 foreclosed; $8M set aside for first 625
check_that_catches: independent recomputation of eligibility inputs; reconciliation of fee inputs vs ledger

title: Epic Sepsis Model: external validation found AUC 0.63 (vendor reported 0.76-0.83); missed 67% of sepsis cases while alerting on 18% of patients
org_or_repo: Epic Systems; Wong et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2021
cause_short: Proprietary model deployed at hundreds of hospitals; at Michigan Medicine (38,455 hospitalizations) sensitivity 33%
detection_how: independent external validation by a hospital research team
check_that_catches: local outcome monitoring vs vendor-reported metric

title: Michigan unemployment system: automated fraud determinations wrong 93% of the time in a state review (late 2013 - mid 2015)
cause_short: System flagged 53,633 fraud cases with penalties; review of a subset found 93% wrong
detection_how: state review after complaints and litigation
cost_stated: penalty fund grew from ~$3M (2011) to ~$155M; $5.4M repaid initially
check_that_catches: sample audit of decisions vs human review; base-rate plausibility (fraud rate jump)

title: California CalREDIE: server crash workaround and an expired certificate silently backlogged ~300,000 COVID test results; governor cited a 20% drop
cause_short: Jul 25 server crash, temporary workaround left in place; Jul 31-Aug 4 expired certificate on a major lab feed; counts kept publishing
detection_how: discrepancy noticed by state officials (not described in source)
cost_stated: undercounted cases during reopening decisions; public health director resigned
check_that_catches: per-source volume check (rows from each lab vs trailing average); freshness per feed

title: Australia Robodebt: averaging annual tax income across fortnights generated ~470,000 wrongful welfare debts (2016-2020); A$1.872B settlement
cause_short: Annual ATO income averaged evenly across fortnights assumed regular earnings; mismatch with fortnightly Centrelink reports produced debts
cost_stated: A$1.872B settlement approved 2021; 470,000 debts repaid; Royal Commission 2023
check_that_catches: assumption check: income regularity test before averaging; distribution of computed debts vs history
evidence_level: reputable-secondary (Wikipedia/Wikiwand; verify vs Royal Commission report)

title: Uber NYC took its commission before sales tax for 2.5 years, underpaying drivers ~$45M (avg ~$900 each)
cause_short: Commission applied to the fare before tax, contrary to the Nov 2014 driver agreement ($20 fare: driver got $13.40 instead of $13.80)
check_that_catches: contract-rule test on payout formula; reconciliation of payouts vs agreement
